title: Structure-Aware Placement and Routing of Multi-Controlled Toffoli on Bivariate Bicycle Code Architectures
authors: Anik Basu Bhaumik, Suman Dutta, Siyi Wang, Anupam Chattopadhyay
abstract: The multi-controlled Toffoli (MCT) gate is a fundamental primitive in quantum circuit design, with applications in quantum arithmetic, cryptanalysis, and algorithmic implementations. Being a high-level logical operation, the efficient decomposition of MCT gates into lower-level netlists has remained a major optimization challenge for decades. While emerging quantum error-correcting codes such as bivariate bicycle (BB) codes drastically reduce fault-tolerance overhead, realizing non-Clifford circuits on modular BB-code architectures introduces complex compilation bottlenecks governed by inter-module routing, factory density, and layout. Consequently, the mapping of MCT gates onto BB-code architectures remains relatively unexplored.   In this paper, we overcome these challenges by mapping optimal-Toffoli-depth MCT decompositions (Dutta et al., PRA, 2025) onto BB-code-based fault-tolerant architectures via direct $\lvert \mathrm{CCZ} \rangle$ state injection from an external magic state factory. We introduce a targeted placement strategy that exploits the binary-tree structure of MCT decompositions to co-locate interacting subtrees. This approach reduces inter-module instruction counts by up to $\mathbf{16.02}\%$ compared to a naive sequential first-fit placement. We also evaluate the impact of factory placement across different topologies, demonstrating that grid-based layouts yield up to a $\mathbf{23.7}\%$ reduction in inter-module instructions relative to linear architectures (Yoder et al., arXiv, 2025). Finally, we validate the practical viability of our compiled circuits by analyzing aggregate execution errors and logical failure probabilities using the bicycle-ISA error estimator bicycle_numerics provided by the Qiskit community, https://github.com/qiskit-community/bicycle-architecture-compiler.
summary: This work tackles the resource overhead of implementing complex MCT gates on BB-code quantum computers. The authors introduce a novel, structure-aware placement strategy that groups interacting circuit components to minimize inter-module communication. This approach significantly reduces routing overhead and provides quantitative estimates of circuit failure probabilities for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the major optimization challenge of efficiently mapping high-level Multi-Controlled Toffoli (MCT) gates onto fault-tolerant quantum architectures based on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes.
main_result: A targeted placement strategy exploiting the binary-tree structure of MCT decompositions reduces inter-module instruction counts by up to 16.02%, and grid-based layouts offer significant routing improvements over linear ones.
method: The authors propose a structure-aware placement strategy combined with direct |CCZ> state injection to map optimal MCT decompositions onto the BB-code architecture, minimizing inter-module routing overhead.
model_or_system: The system is a fault-tolerant quantum computer utilizing Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes, which are a type of qLDPC code. The workload involves implementing MCT gates, requiring the management of magic-state factories for non-Clifford operations.
key_observables: Inter-module instruction count (routing overhead), aggregate execution errors (E), and circuit failure probabilities (P_fail).
important_parameters: The grouping factor (k), the physical error rate (p), and the topology (grid vs. linear).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the availability of optimal-Toffoli-depth MCT decompositions and relies on the Qiskit community's bicycle_numerics error estimator.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of routing performance between linear and grid factory placements, and show the calculated aggregate error and circuit failure probabilities as a function of circuit size (n) and physical error rate (p).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the difficulty of mapping MCT gates onto BB-code architectures. It then introduces the targeted placement strategy, detailing how grouping subtrees reduces routing overhead. Finally, it validates the approach by analyzing aggregate error and failure probabilities under different topological constraints.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation, the optimization techniques—specifically the graph-based placement heuristics and resource estimation—are relevant to designing complex physical implementations of quantum circuits.
